vh-1-0-2-1.title: The Greasy Tallow-Skin
vh-1-0-2-1.text:
Mistress Garrow shoves a greasy tallow-skin into your coat-pocket with strict orders to grease your boot-seams before the middle stairs. The buttery corridor smells heavily of soured milk and damp flagstones, a stale refuge against the howling drafts outside. You finger the stoppered leather flask, wondering if the grease will hold back the slush of the lower runs or merely attract the mountain grit.

Weighing your next move, you consider the icy drop awaiting you beyond the walls.

vh-1-0-2-2.title: Frozen Ruts and Carts
vh-1-0-2-2.text:
Iron-shod cart wheels crack the frozen ruts beside the north curtain wall while a teamster curses his stumbling mare on the slope. The beast's breath plumes white against the dark grey granite of Vesperhold, and the weight of your burden pulls sharply at your shoulders. You steady the heavy bronze Clapper in its padded cradle, matching your stance to the shudder of the mountain wind.

The cart groans forward, clearing a narrow path for your descent.
exits: Catch your breath near the mast

vh-1-0-2-3.title: The Cable Court Toll
vh-1-0-2-3.text:
Under the shadow of the winch-tower, a Cable Court bailiff blocks your path to demand a toll-token for the bronze you carry down to the valley. His brass-trimmed badge catches the pale mountain glare, and his hand rests casually upon a heavy ledger. You shift your weight, feeling the faint, stubborn hum of the metal against your spine as you weigh a sharp reply against compliance.

The wind whistles through the iron pulleys overhead, urging you to decide.
exits: Test your grip on the ice

vh-1-0-2-4.title: Plums and Barley Prices
vh-1-0-2-4.text:
A terrace miller thrusts a bag of dried plums into your pouch at the junction of the upper lych-gate, begging news of barley prices in Lowgate. Her fingers are calloused from years of tending high-altitude wind-crops, and her eyes betray the quiet hunger of the terraces. You nod noncommittally, tucking the sweet fruit close to your ribs while the bitter air bites your cheeks.

The path splits before you into shadow and frost.

vh-1-0-2-5.title: The Glacier Gust
vh-1-0-2-5.text:
A sudden gust of wind off the glacier nearly lifts you from your boots in the open courtyard, forcing you to lean your heavy frame into the rock-face. The bronze Clapper hums a deeper note against your spine as the pressure shifts, echoing the vast emptiness of the precipice below. You wait out the squall with your gloved hands clawed into the limestone crevices.

The gale subsides just enough for you to pick a route.

vh-1-0-2-6.title: Sheep-Dip and Crooked Wood
vh-1-0-2-6.text:
Wet fleece and dung fill the air as you pass the sheep-dip pens, where an old shepherd waves a crooked hazel stick toward the grey stairs below. The animals crowd against the wooden hurdles, steaming in the morning chill while their bells clatter a dull accompaniment to your thoughts. You glance down the winding stone track, measuring the distance to the first cloud-bank.

The shepherd turns back to his flock without a word more.

vh-1-0-2-7.title: Pewter Charm on Stone
vh-1-0-2-7.text:
A nervous novice presses a pewter charm of St. Jude into your palm by the frozen fountain to ward off the rock-slides on the Ninety Steps. The metal is bitterly cold against your skin, stamped with the crude image of a fisherman and a heavy oar. You slip the trinket into your mitten, offering a brief, silent nod to the boy before looking down the dizzying drop.

The fountain ice cracks with a sharp, pistol-like report.

vh-1-0-2-8.title: Charcoal-Burner's Yard
vh-1-0-2-8.text:
Soot-stained lads roll pine logs through the slush in the charcoal-burner's yard while you sidestep a rolling roundwood with the heavy Clapper swaying. The sweet, acrid scent of charred wood cuts through the biting mountain air, clinging to your woollen tunic. You keep your balance on the slick mud, eyes fixed on the narrow exit between the stacked timber cribs.

The lads shout a rough warning as another log breaks loose.

vh-1-0-2-9.title: Canvas and Icicles
vh-1-0-2-9.text:
You adjust the canvas rain-hood over your cradle under the timber pentice of the buttery stores to shield the bronze tongue from dripping icicles. Water droplets strike the heavy cloth with dull ticks like a clock running down, while the metal within answers with a faint, sympathetic tremor. You secure the drawstrings with numb fingers, checking the lashings one last time.

The path ahead drops sharply into the grey haze.

vh-1-0-2-10.title: Lime-Kiln Dust
vh-1-0-2-10.text:
White lime dust coats your boots as you skirt a steaming heap of slaking stone beside the kiln, while the mountain air bites your ears. The heat from the pit radiates against your freezing side, a brief and deceptive comfort before the long cold descent. You cough once against the alkaline haze, wiping your spectacles with a frosted sleeve.

The trail continues past the smoking enclosure into the wind.
exits: Watch the kitten on the sled
